title: [Mouse Without Borders] Impossible to run without elevated privileges, Impossible to change layout

actions.label: Confirm non-elevated device layout edit
actions.note: Ask for the one clarification that separates intended elevated-session behavior from a real MWB layout-editing bug.

comment.body:
I re-checked the current Mouse Without Borders settings code, and the message you quoted is real: drag-drop layout editing is intentionally disabled whenever the Settings session is still **elevated** because WinUI 3 drag-drop is unstable in that mode. The key missing detail is whether you retried after a **full non-elevated restart**.

1. **Please turn off Run as administrator, fully exit every PowerToys process, start PowerToys again without elevation, and confirm whether drag-drop layout editing is still blocked.**
2. **Please confirm whether any other elevated PowerToys instance or service-managed session is still running when you test again.**

If the layout editor is still blocked in a truly non-elevated session, that would be a much stronger MWB bug than the current report can prove.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders intentionally disables drag-drop layout editing while Settings is elevated, so the open question is whether the reporter ever retried after a full non-elevated restart.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.101.2362 and targets Mouse Without Borders.
The visible message quoted by the reporter matches a current Settings UI string in src/settings-ui/Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw.
MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs explicitly sets drag-drop availability from `!IsElevated` and documents a WinUI3 crash reason.
inferences: If the reporter toggled the run-as-admin option but kept using an already elevated session, the current restriction message would persist by design.
Only a clean non-elevated relaunch that still leaves layout editing disabled would justify a new bug investigation.
issue_context.analysis: This needs a precise clarification, not design work. The source already explains why the UI blocks drag-drop while elevated.
initial_investigation: Confirmed the quoted restriction message in Settings.UI/Strings/en-us/Resources.resw.
Reviewed MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs and confirmed layout drag/drop is intentionally disabled whenever `IsElevated` is true.
Confirmed the comment references a known WinUI3 drag-drop crash, so current behavior is at least partly deliberate.

information_gaps.information: Whether layout editing is still blocked after exiting every PowerToys process and restarting PowerToys non-elevated.
information_gaps.why_needed: That distinguishes the intended elevated-session restriction from a genuine bug in non-elevated layout editing.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please turn off Run as administrator, fully exit all PowerToys processes, start PowerToys again without elevation, and confirm whether drag-drop layout editing is still blocked.

information_gaps.information: Whether another elevated PowerToys instance or service-managed session remains active when the reporter retries.
information_gaps.why_needed: A leftover elevated instance would keep `IsElevated` true even after the setting was changed.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please confirm whether the retried session is the only running PowerToys instance and whether Mouse Without Borders is using service mode.

judgment.rationale: The current source intentionally disables Mouse Without Borders drag-drop layout editing whenever the Settings process is elevated because of a WinUI3 drag-drop crash, so the key missing discriminator is whether the reporter actually restarted into a non-elevated session before retrying.
evidence: The Settings UI resource text already says drag and drop is not possible while PowerToys is elevated and asks the user to restart without elevation to edit the device layout.
MouseWithoutBordersViewModel.cs constructs device thumbnails with `CanDragDrop = !IsElevated` and comments that dragging while elevated crashes on WinUI3.
The report says layout editing is impossible even after turning off “run as administrator”, but it does not say whether all PowerToys processes were fully restarted non-elevated.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for one clean non-elevated restart result and install-scope clarification before treating this as a new MWB bug.

fix_assessment.rationale: Today’s visible restriction is an intentional UI safety guard; the unresolved question is whether the reporter is still elevated after toggling settings.
